Theorem
[Space-time mean value property on a manifold] Source: chow-et-al-ricci-flow-part-iii:page-0390, chow-et-al-ricci-flow-part-iii:page-0391, chow-et-al-ricci-flow-part-iii:page-0392, chow-et-al-ricci-flow-part-iii:page-0393, chow-et-al-ricci-flow-part-iii:page-0394 ↗ def:chow-iii-gamma-a-regular-function 1. ch26:26.41\group Heat Balls

Suppose $H(y,y, au )\le C/f( au )$ for a $(\gamma ,A)$-regular $f:(0,\infty ) o (0,\infty )$. If $u_t=\Delta u$, then for sufficiently small $r>0$, $E_r(x_0,t_0)$ is relatively compact and \[ u(x_0,t_0)= rac1{r^n}\iint _{E_r(x_0,t_0)}u(y,t) | abla \log H(x_0,y,t_0-t)|^2\, d\mu (y)dt. \]
Proof

\sketch The diagonal hypothesis yields a Gaussian off-diagonal bound, hence compact heat-ball slices and finite integrals. The coarea formula and $\psi _{r,t}+\Delta \psi _r=-| abla \psi _r|^2$ give

\[ rac d{dr}I(r)= rac n{r^{n+1}}\iint _{E_r}\psi _r(\Delta u-u_t)\, d\mu dt. \]

Thus $I$ is constant for heat solutions, and heat-kernel asymptotics give $\lim _{r\downarrow 0}I(r)=u(x_0,t_0)$.

□
